{{Short description|None}}
This '''glossary of linear algebra''' is a list of definitions and terms relevant to the field of [[linear algebra]], the branch of mathematics concerned with linear equations and their representations as [[vector space]]s.

For a glossary related to the generalization of vector spaces through [[Module (mathematics)|module]]s, see [[glossary of module theory]].

{{Compact TOC}}

== A ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|1=[[affine transformation]]}}
{{defn|1=A composition of functions consisting of a linear transformation between vector spaces followed by a translation.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=7}} Equivalently, a function between vector spaces that preserves affine combinations.}}
{{term|1=[[affine combination]]}}
{{defn|1=A linear combination in which the sum of the coefficients is 1.}}
{{glossary end}}

== B ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|1=basis|2=[[Basis (linear algebra)|basis]]}}
{{defn|1=In a {{gli|vector space}}, a {{gli|linear dependence|linearly independent}} set of {{gli|vector}}s spanning the whole vector space.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=27}}}}
{{term|basis vector|[[basis vector]]}}
{{defn|1=An element of a given [[#basis|basis]] of a vector space.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=27}}}}
{{term|1=bilinear form|2=[[bilinear form]]}}
{{defn|1=On vector space ''V'' over field ''K'', a bilinear form is a function <math>B : V \times V \to K</math> that is linear in each variable.}}
{{glossary end}}

== C ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|column vector|[[Row and column vectors|column vector]]}}
{{defn|1=A {{gli|matrix}} with only one column.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=66}}}}
{{term|[[complex number]]}}
{{defn|1=An element of a complex plane}}
{{term|[[complex plane]]}}
{{defn|1=A {{gli|linear algebra}} over the real numbers with {{gli|basis}} {1, i }, where i is an {{gli|imaginary unit}}<ref>Curtis, page 155</ref>}}
{{term|1=[[coordinate vector]]}}
{{defn|1=The [[tuple]] of the [[coordinates]] of a {{gli|vector}} on a {{gli|basis}}.}}
{{term|1=[[covector]]}}
{{defn|1=An element of the {{gli|dual space}} of a {{gli|vector space}}, (that is a {{gli|linear form}}), identified to an element of the vector space through an [[inner product]].}}
{{glossary end}}

== D ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|1=[[determinant]]}}
{{defn|1=The unique scalar function over {{gli|square matrix|square matrices}} which is distributive over {{gli|matrix multiplication}}, multilinear in the rows and columns, and takes the value of <math>1</math> for the {{gli|identity matrix}}.<ref>Curtis, page 116</ref>}}
{{term|1=[[diagonal matrix]]}}
{{defn|1=A matrix in which only the entries on the main diagonal are non-zero.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=263}}}}
{{term|dimension|[[Dimension (vector space)|dimension]]}}
{{defn|1=The number of elements of any {{gli|basis}} of a {{gli|vector space}}.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=27}}}}
{{term|1=[[dot product]]}}
{{defn|1=Given two vectors of the same length, the dot product is the sum of the products of their corresponding indices.}}
{{term|1=[[dual space]]}}
{{defn|1=The {{gli|vector space}} of all {{gli|linear form}}s on a given vector space.{{sfn|James|James|1992|pages=80,135}}}}
{{glossary end}}

== E ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|Elementary matrix|[[elementary matrix]]}}
{{defn|{{gli|Square matrix}} that differs from the {{gli|identity matrix}} by at most one entry}}
{{glossary end}}
== H ==
{{term|hyperbolic unit}}
{{defn|no=1|1=An operator (''x, y'') → (''y, x''), reflecting the plane in the 45° diagonal}}
{{defn|no=2|1=In a {{gli|linear algebra}}, a {{gli|linear map}} which when composed with itself yields the identity}}

== I ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|Identity matrix|[[identity matrix]]{{anchor|identity matrix}}}}
{{defn|1=A diagonal matrix all of the diagonal elements of which are equal to <math>1</math>.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=263}}}}
{{term|[[imaginary unit]]}}
{{defn|no=1|1=An operator (''x, y'') → (''y, –x''), rotating the plane 90° counterclockwise}}
{{defn|no=2|1=In a {{gli|linear algebra}}, a {{gli|linear map}} which when composed with itself produces the negative of the identity}}
{{term|1=[[inverse matrix]]}}
{{defn|1=Of a matrix <math>A</math>, another matrix <math>B</math> such that <math>A</math> multiplied by <math>B</math> and <math>B</math> multiplied by <math>A</math> both equal the identity matrix.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=263}}}}
{{term|Isotropic vector|[[isotropic vector]]}}
{{defn|1=In a vector space with a [[quadratic form]], a non-zero vector for which the form is zero.}}
{{term|1=[[isotropic quadratic form]]}}
{{defn|1=A vector space with a quadratic form which has a {{gli|null vector}}.}}
{{glossary end}}

== L ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|1=[[linear algebra]]}}
{{defn|no=1|1=The branch of mathematics that deals with vectors, vector spaces, linear transformations and systems of linear equations.}}
{{defn|no=2|1=A {{gli|vector space}} that has a [[binary operation]] making it a [[ring (mathematics)|ring]]. This linear algebra is also known as an [[algebra over a field]].<ref>Dickson, page 3</ref>}}
{{term|1=[[linear combination]]}}
{{defn|1=A sum, each of whose summands is an appropriate vector times an appropriate scalar (or ring element).{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=251}}}}
{{term|1=[[linear dependence]]}}
{{defn|1=A linear dependence of a tuple of vectors <math display=inline>\vec v_1,\ldots,\vec v_n</math> is a nonzero tuple of scalar coefficients <math display=inline>c_1,\ldots,c_n</math> for which the linear combination <math display=inline>c_1\vec v_1+\cdots+c_n\vec v_n</math> equals <math display=inline>\vec0</math>.}}
{{term|1=[[linear equation]]}}
{{defn|1=A [[polynomial equation]] of degree one (such as <math>x = 2y - 7</math>).{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=252}}}}
{{term|1=[[linear form]]}}
{{defn|1=A {{gli|linear map}} from a {{gli|vector space}} to its field of scalars.{{sfn|Bourbaki|1989|page=232}}}}
{{term|1=[[linear independence]]}}
{{defn|1=Property of being not {{gli|linear dependence|linearly dependent}}.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=111}}}}
{{term|1=[[linear map]]}}
{{defn|1=A [[function (mathematics)|function]] between {{gli|vector space}}s which respects addition and scalar multiplication.}}
{{term|1=[[linear transformation]]}}
{{defn|1=A {{gli|linear map}} whose [[domain of a function|domain]] and [[codomain]] are equal; it is generally supposed to be [[inverse function|invertible]].}}
{{glossary end}}

== M ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|matrix|[[Matrix (mathematics)|matrix]]}}
{{defn|1=Rectangular arrangement of numbers or other [[mathematical object]]s.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=263}} A matrix is written ''A'' = (a<sub>i, j</sub>), where a<sub>i, j</sub> is the entry at row i and column j.}}
{{term|1=[[matrix multiplication]]}}
{{defn|1=If a matrix ''A'' has the same number of columns as does matrix ''B'' of rows, then a product ''C'' = ''AB'' may be formed with ''c''<sub>i, j</sub> equal to the {{gli|dot product}} of row i of ''A'' with column j of ''B''.}}
{{glossary end}}

== N ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|1=[[null vector]]}}
{{defn |no=1 |1=Another term for an {{gli|isotropic vector}}.}}
{{defn |no=2 |1=Another term for a {{gli|zero vector}}.}}
{{glossary end}}

== O ==
{{glossary}}

{{term|1=[[orthogonality (mathematics)|orthogonality]]}}
{{defn|1=Two vectors ''u'' and ''v'' are orthogonal with respect to a {{gli|bilinear form}} ''B'' when ''B''(''u,v'') = 0.}}
{{term|1=[[orthonormality]]}}
{{defn|1= A set of vectors is orthonormal when they are all {{gli|unit vector}}s and are pairwise orthogonal.}}
{{term|1=[[orthogonal matrix]]}}
{{defn|1= A real square matrix with rows (or columns) that form an orthonormal set.}}
{{glossary end}}

== R ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|1=[[Row and column vectors|row vector]]}}
{{defn|1=A matrix with only one row.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=263}}}}
{{glossary end}}

== S ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|1=[[scalar (mathematics)|scalar]]}}
{{defn|1=A scalar is an element of a [[field (mathematics)|field]] used in the definition of a {{gli|vector space}}.}}
{{term|1=[[singular-value decomposition]]}}
{{defn|1=a factorization of an <math>m \times n</math> complex matrix {{math|'''M'''}} as <math>\mathbf{U\Sigma V^*}</math>, where {{math|'''U'''}} is an <math>m \times m</math> complex [[unitary matrix]], <math>\mathbf{\Sigma}</math> is an <math>m \times n</math> [[rectangular diagonal matrix]] with non-negative real numbers on the diagonal, and {{math|'''V'''}} is an <math>n \times n</math> complex unitary matrix.{{sfn|Williams|2014|page=407}}}}
{{term|spectrum|[[Spectrum of a matrix|spectrum]]}}
{{defn|Set of the [[eigenvalue]]s of a matrix.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=389}}}}
{{term|[[split-complex number]]}}
{{defn|1=An element of a split-complex plane.}}
{{term|split-complex plane}}
{{defn|1=A {{gli|linear algebra}} over the real numbers with {{gli|basis}} {1, j }, where j is a {{gli|hyperbolic unit}}.}}
{{term|square matrix|[[square matrix]]}}
{{defn|1=A matrix having the same number of rows as columns.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=263}}}}
{{glossary end}}

== T ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|1=[[transpose]]}}
{{defn|The transpose of an n × m matrix ''M'' is an m × n matrix ''M ''<sup>T</sup> obtained by using the rows of ''M'' for the columns of ''M ''<sup>T</sup>.}}
{{glossary end}}

== U ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|1=[[unit vector]]}}
{{defn|1=a vector in a normed vector space whose [[Norm (mathematics)|norm]] is 1, or a [[Euclidean vector]] of length one.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=463}}}}
{{glossary end}}

== V ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|1=[[Vector (mathematics and physics)|vector]]}} 
{{defn|1=A directed quantity, one with both magnitude and direction.|no=1}}
{{defn|An element of a vector space.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=441}}|no=2}}
{{term|1=[[vector space]]}}
{{defn|1=A [[set (mathematics)|set]], whose elements can be added together, and multiplied by elements of a [[field (mathematics)|field]] (this is [[scalar multiplication]]); the set must be an [[abelian group]] under addition, and the scalar multiplication must be a [[linear map]].{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=442}}}}
{{glossary end}}

== Z ==
{{glossary}}
{{term|1=[[zero vector]]}}
{{defn|1=The [[additive identity]] in a vector space. In a [[normed vector space]], it is the unique vector of norm zero. In a [[Euclidean vector space]], it is the unique vector of length zero.{{sfn|James|James|1992|page=452}}}}
{{glossary end}}
